name: Amasra Peninsula
tagline: The old town inside the castle walls
description: The headland where Amasra actually sits, ringed by Genoese and Byzantine walls with narrow lanes, the museum, guesthouses and views over both bays. Everything on the peninsula is within a ten-minute walk and the whole point of being here is being on it.
bestFor: Anyone here for the town itself rather than a base
pros: Castle walls, museum and both harbours on foot
The most atmospheric accommodation in town
Views over the Black Sea from both sides
cons: Older buildings have the weakest internet
Packed with domestic tourists in July and August
Steep narrow lanes and no parking

name: Buyuk Liman
tagline: The big harbour and the main beach
description: The larger of the two bays, with the fishing boats, the harbourside fish restaurants and the town beach. It is where the evening happens in summer and where most of the pensions and small hotels face the water.
bestFor: Summer stays wanting the beach and the fish restaurants
pros: The town beach and the restaurant strip
Fishing boats land the catch here
cons: Crowded and loud in high season
Prices rise sharply in July and August

name: Kucuk Liman
tagline: The small harbour, quieter on the other side
description: The second bay on the western side of the peninsula, smaller, calmer and with a rockier shore. Fewer visitors reach it and the guesthouses here are cheaper, with the walk over the neck of the peninsula to the main harbour taking about five minutes.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the town without the summer crowd
pros: Noticeably quieter than the main harbour
Cheaper guesthouses for the same location
cons: Still busy at the peak of the season

name: Bartin
tagline: The provincial town twenty minutes inland
description: The provincial centre south of Amasra, a working Turkish town with the university, the hospital, the main bus connections and the services the coast lacks. Rents are considerably lower and anyone staying for months rather than weeks generally ends up looking here.
bestFor: Long stays needing services, a hospital and a real rental market
pros: Open all year rather than seasonal
cons: No sea and none of Amasra's charm
Twenty minutes to the coast by road
Entirely Turkish-speaking, with no visitor infrastructure
